A **desktop condition read** uses era, construction, documents and public signals to triage a shortlist and direct later questions. A physical inspection then examines accessible conditions at the property. Read how a [desktop property report and a physical inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/desktop-vs-physical-report) work in sequence.

## Insurance condition surveys
An insurer may request property information or its own survey before offering or renewing cover. Ask what document and evidence it requires before commissioning one. The [home condition and insurance guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/home-condition-and-insurance) covers underwriting, rebuild cost, exclusions, maintenance and evidence.

## Dilapidation reports: before the neighbours dig
A dilapidation report creates a dated baseline before nearby construction, demolition or excavation begins. It records existing cracks, paths and other relevant conditions for later comparison. Arrange it before work starts and pair it with [the wall-crack guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/cracks-structural-or-cosmetic).

### When you need a dilapidation report, and what it records

The most common trigger is building work next door: a demolition, excavation for a basement or pool, a new house built close to the boundary, or major works on shared walls. Councils and builders may also require one before large projects, and some owners commission their own before works on their street. Arrange it before any work starts, because a report done afterwards cannot show what was already there.

**What a useful dilapidation report records**

| Item | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Existing cracks, with location, width and photographs | The baseline for comparing any later cracking |
| Floor levels, door and window operation | Shows whether movement has happened since |
| Paths, driveways, fences, retaining walls and paving | Ground-level damage near excavation is common |
| Wet areas, ceilings and roof, where accessible | Leaks and cracking can follow vibration and movement |
| The date, the scope and what was not accessible | Defines what the baseline can and cannot prove |

In Victoria, the [Building and Plumbing Commission](https://www.bpc.vic.gov.au/home-owners/home-renovation-and-building-essentials/protecting-adjoining-properties) explains protection work: where proposed building work could affect an adjoining property, the builder may need to carry out protection work and notify the neighbour, and a record of the adjoining property's condition is commonly made before work starts. Other states handle it differently, so check your state's rules. If you receive a notice about work next door, read it promptly, keep copies, and keep your own dated photos of the parts of your home nearest the work. Keep the report itself in your [home record](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/keeping-a-record-of-your-home).

> Note: A dilapidation report records condition. It does not decide who caused later damage or who pays; that may need further technical investigation and advice.

## Property condition assessments: the commercial cousin
A *property condition assessment* is more common in commercial property, where investors and lenders assess an asset and its likely capital needs. For a home, maintain the equivalent evidence through [a current property record](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/keeping-a-record-of-your-home).

## Which one do you need?
- **Starting or ending a lease:** the rental condition report, done thoroughly, with photos.
- **Serious about buying a specific property:** the pre-purchase building and pest inspection.
- **Weighing several properties, or wanting an independent early read:** the desktop condition read.
- **Insurer asking questions, or an older home being priced for cover:** the insurance condition survey, plus a current condition record of your own.
- **Major construction starting next door:** the dilapidation report, arranged before the works begin.

## Commission the question before choosing the report
Start with the decision and the intended recipient. A lender, insurer, buyer or neighbouring owner may need different evidence, author qualifications and reliance terms. Ask the recipient to specify what it will accept before paying for a document. A polished report with the wrong scope can leave the original request unanswered.

Write a short brief: property and areas concerned; decision and deadline; known symptoms; available documents; required access; questions that need answering; and who is to use the result. Identify whether you need a broad visual assessment, a specialist investigation, a baseline record or a repair and capital plan. If more than one is needed, agree their sequence so the later professional can use the earlier evidence.

**Four questions that stop unlike reports being compared**

| Question | What to look for | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What was assessed? | Property identity, areas, elements and expressly excluded systems | A lot inspection may omit the shared building |
| How was it assessed? | Physical inspection, documents, photographs, testing or sampling | Different methods support different conclusions |
| When and under what conditions? | Inspection date, weather, occupancy and access | Dry conditions or blocked access may limit evidence |
| Who may use it? | Client, purpose, permitted recipients and reliance terms | Receiving a PDF does not automatically make you an authorised relying party |

## Tenancy evidence has a particular purpose
[Victoria's condition-report guidance](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/renting/rent-bond-bills-and-condition-reports/condition-reports) explains how the rental provider and renter record entry condition and use the record in disputes. Check the property's current state process, template and return deadline. Label photographs by location and retain copies with any corrections. This evidence concerns the tenancy's condition record; completing the form does not amount to a specialist structural investigation.

If a room has an existing stain, record its visible location and extent rather than writing an unverified cause such as 'old roof leak'. Report a repair issue through the applicable tenancy process as well. The entry form, a repair notification and a later trade finding can all matter, but they are different records. Keep them connected without rewriting the original observation after the cause is identified.

## A baseline is useful without proving causation
For neighbouring works, a useful baseline needs identifiable locations, dated photographs, visible defects, measurement where appropriate and clear access limitations. Comparable later observations are easier to interpret than photographs taken from unrelated angles. A pre-existing crack can change, and a new crack can have more than one possible cause. Timing and comparison inform an investigation; they do not alone allocate liability.

Specific legal processes may apply. In Victoria, [BPC's protection-work guidance](https://www.bpc.vic.gov.au/home-owners/home-renovation-and-building-essentials/protecting-adjoining-properties) describes a survey of the adjoining property's existing condition, prepared with the adjoining owner and agreed before protection work. Ask the relevant surveyor or adviser whether that process applies; commissioning a generic commercial report is not automatically the same as satisfying its requirements.

## Price the scope and the follow-up
Obtain a current written quote for the actual property. Compare access arrangements, buildings included, timber-pest scope, specialist input, testing, turnaround, clarification and any reinspection. A lower price can reflect a narrower service rather than a saving for the same question. There is no useful universal price for every document called a property condition report.

Ask what happens if the first visit cannot access a critical area or identifies a specialist question. Is another visit included, separately priced or outside the engagement? A report that recommends further investigation may be doing its job correctly. Budget for the decision pathway rather than assuming the first report must settle every uncertainty. Use [the report-reading guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/how-to-read-a-building-and-pest-report) to turn findings and exclusions into specific follow-up questions.

## Know what makes an old report less useful
There is no single age at which every report becomes useless or reliable. Relevance changes with purpose, intervening works, leaks, storms, occupancy and new access. Ask the author or proposed recipient whether an update is needed for your decision. An old report can remain valuable historical evidence while being inadequate to establish today's condition.

## Worked example: two reports describe different things
**Illustrative reasoning example, not an inspected property.** A buyer receives a tenancy entry report describing a room as clean and undamaged, and a pre-purchase report noting an inaccessible subfloor beneath it. They read the tenancy form as reassurance about the whole room's construction.

The first report records visible tenancy condition at its date. The second expressly leaves an area uninspected. These statements do not contradict each other and neither establishes the condition of concealed floor supports. Ask whether suitable access and further inspection can be arranged within the buyer's decision timetable.

If access remains unavailable, preserve that uncertainty in the decision. A desktop review might help frame construction questions, but it cannot replace the missing observation. Choosing the next evidence by the unanswered question is more useful than choosing whichever report has the most reassuring title.

Keep conclusions at the level the evidence supports: observed, reported, inferred or confirmed. An unavailable document is a gap in the record; it does not prove the work was never done.

> Note: A condition report is dated evidence. Keep it with later inspections, repairs, photographs and records so the next decision starts from the current building.

## Frequently asked questions
### Which Australian Standard covers pre-purchase inspections?
AS 4349.1-2007 covers pre-purchase inspections of residential buildings, and AS 4349.3 covers timber pest inspections. They set a minimum scope, a visual inspection of safely accessible areas and a structured report.

### What is a property condition report?
A dated record of selected property conditions. The term can describe tenancy forms, pre-purchase inspections, desktop reviews, insurer surveys or dilapidation reports. Confirm the purpose, method, scope and reliance terms.

### Is a property condition report the same as a building inspection?
For buyers, the phrase often means a pre-purchase building inspection. It also names rental entry and exit forms, insurance surveys and dilapidation reports, so confirm the purpose and scope.

### How much does a property condition report cost?
There is no single price across these different services. For a commissioned report, obtain a current scoped quote covering the property, access, specialist work and follow-up. For a tenancy condition record, follow the applicable jurisdiction’s process.

### What is an insurance condition survey?
A property assessment requested or accepted for underwriting or risk review. Confirm the required scope with the insurer first. Policy wording and insurer assessment control the outcome.

### What is a property condition assessment?
Mostly a commercial-property term: an assessment, commissioned by an investor or lender, of an asset’s condition and the capital it is likely to need over a holding period. The residential equivalent of the habit is a current condition read of your home, kept up to date over time.

### Do I need a dilapidation report if construction is starting next door?
It creates a dated baseline for later comparison. Arrange it before excavation, demolition or construction begins.

### Can I rely on a report commissioned by someone else?
Check its purpose and contractual reliance terms with the author and your adviser. Possession of a copy alone does not establish a right of reliance.

### How long is a property condition report valid?
There is no universal period. Purpose, access and intervening changes matter; ask the author or intended recipient whether a current assessment or update is required.

### Does a dilapidation report prove nearby work caused damage?
It provides baseline evidence for comparison. Causation and responsibility may require further technical investigation and legal advice.

## Method
A report-selection guide distinguishing purpose, evidence method, scope, reliance and pricing. Victorian tenancy and protection-work examples are explicitly local, not national rules.

## Limitations
General Australian guidance only. Contracts, statutes, policies, site conditions and professional scopes vary; obtain advice for the property and decision in front of you.

## Sources

- [Protecting adjoining properties](https://www.bpc.vic.gov.au/home-owners/home-renovation-and-building-essentials/protecting-adjoining-properties) — Building and Plumbing Commission Victoria; accessed 2026-09-07

- [AS 4349.1-2007 Inspection of buildings, Part 1: Pre-purchase inspections, residential buildings](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) — Standards Australia; accessed 2026-07-20

sections.heading: Opening
sections.markdown:
### Find the person who can answer your question
- **Building professional:** For defects, structure, drainage and moisture you can see
- **Environmental assessor:** For sampling and the indoor environment, with a defined scope
- **Health practitioner:** For symptoms and medical diagnosis

_If it is about your health, the right professional is medical._

sections.heading: Start with the question that is worrying you
sections.markdown:
“Building biologist” can mean moisture and mould investigation, indoor-air sampling, lead or chemical testing, electromagnetic-field measurement, drinking-water testing or a whole-home package. Tell each provider what you have noticed and what decision you need to make. That gives them a fair chance to quote the right work.

**Choose the professional by the decision you need to make**

| Question | Useful first professional | What the work should produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where is water entering or condensing? | Building inspector, building consultant or suitably experienced moisture investigator | Moisture pathway, affected materials, access limits and repair brief |
| What is present in air, dust or a surface? | Indoor environmental professional or occupational hygienist with an appropriate sampling plan | Defined method, chain of custody, laboratory result and interpretation limits |
| Has mould remediation achieved its scope? | Independent post-remediation verifier | Pre-agreed acceptance criteria and verification report |
| Are symptoms connected with the home? | Registered health practitioner | Medical assessment informed by relevant building results |
| Is cracking, movement or another defect structurally significant? | Building inspector, then structural engineer if indicated | Building evidence and, where required, engineering diagnosis |

sections.heading: Dated published pricing
sections.markdown:
These three provider pages were checked on 7 September 2026. They describe different packages, not a national price range. Provider prices are reported here as commercial observations; their inclusion is not an endorsement of a provider’s health claims or testing recommendations.

**Provider fee examples checked 7 September 2026; confirm tax treatment and address-specific scope**

| Provider example | Published fee | Important inclusions or additions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Building Biology NSW](https://buildingbiologynsw.com.au/service/the-complete-healthy-home-inspection/) | $850 single storey; up to $1,000 double storey | $140 per sample; comprehensive report separately $850; confirm GST and other charges |
| [Wave Building Biology](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) | $990 including GST | Mould assessment $990 including GST; sample analysis $120 each; confirm tax basis of extras |
| [Buildingbiology Services Australia](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) | About $970 standard; $1,660 detailed | Specified samples and reporting; travel additional. Confirm laboratory inclusions and GST for the selected package |

Property size, access, site time, sample count, laboratory fees, travel, report depth, urgency and return visits determine the final cost. Give each consultant the same written problem and ask for the complete expected fee.

sections.heading: The quote checklist
sections.markdown:
- **Question and scope:** the rooms, history, suspected pathway and decision the report must support.
- **Investigation method:** visual inspection, moisture meter, thermal imaging, borescope, sampling or another defined method, and its limitations.
- **Sampling plan:** sample type, number, locations, controls, independent laboratory, chain of custody and the fee for each additional sample.
- **Deliverable:** verbal advice, short findings, comprehensive report, repair scope or post-remediation criteria.
- **Independence:** whether the assessor also sells remediation, products or follow-on work.
- **Professional standing:** relevant training, experience, professional indemnity and the laboratory’s accreditation for the analysis requested.

sections.heading: Check training and laboratory scope
sections.markdown: The [National Training Register lists 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology as current](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT). Verify the practitioner’s actual training and experience for the service commissioned. A qualification is not medical registration or blanket authority for every specialist task. For testing, check the laboratory’s relevant analytical scope and require the method, sample provenance and interpretation limits.

sections.heading: Mould: find moisture before chasing species
sections.markdown:
Mould growth requires moisture. [NSW Health](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx) and the [Victorian Department of Health](https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/mould-and-your-health) emphasise moisture control and safe clean-up. Use sampling for a defined purpose such as characterising contamination, documenting a dispute or checking remediation.

[NSW Health says testing is generally unnecessary for visible household mould](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx), while concealed or unresolved problems can warrant specialist assessment. A DIY culture result alone cannot establish the source, full extent or individual health significance. Start with [the moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home) and a defined question.

sections.heading: EMF measurement and health questions
sections.markdown: An instrument can measure an electromagnetic field, but the quantity, frequency, method and comparison standard must fit the question. [ARPANSA states that evidence does not establish low-level EMF exposure as the cause of attributed hypersensitivity symptoms](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/understanding-radiation/radiation-sources/more-radiation-sources/electromagnetic-hypersensitivity), while recognising that symptoms are real and recommending medical assessment. A measured field is not evidence that a home caused illness. Do not treat a consultant’s private target as an Australian exposure standard.

sections.heading: When specialist environmental work is proportionate
sections.markdown:
- **Recurring or widespread mould** where the water source or affected extent remains unclear.
- **A concealed or complex water event**, including a flood, long-running leak or contaminated cavity.
- **A formal dispute, insurance or remediation process** that needs an agreed sampling or verification protocol.
- **A vulnerable occupant** where a health practitioner wants better environmental information to support clinical care.
- **A specific exposure question** that can be measured against a recognised method and standard.

For an ordinary pre-purchase decision, start with a qualified [building and pest inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). Add environmental work for specific questions left unresolved.

sections.heading: Decide what a sample could change before buying it
sections.markdown:
Write the question before choosing the test. Are you trying to find a moisture source, characterise a particular material, document the extent of contamination or check an agreed remediation outcome? Ask how the proposed sample and method answer that question, what comparison is appropriate and what an inconclusive result would mean. A package with more samples is not automatically a more useful investigation.

Keep the field context with the laboratory result in your [home record](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/keeping-a-record-of-your-home): date, room or location, material, recent cleaning or disturbance, sampling method and relevant conditions. Ask the assessor what the sample represents and what it does not. A result from one sampled location should not quietly become a conclusion about every concealed part of a building or the cause of an occupant's symptoms.

**A result and the separate decision it leaves open**

| Evidence | What it may contribute | What still needs assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visible staining or growth | A location and extent to investigate | Moisture source, concealed effects and appropriate response |
| Laboratory result | Information about the submitted sample using the stated method | Representativeness, interpretation and building-wide significance |
| Instrument reading | A measured quantity under particular conditions | Whether the method and comparison answer the original question |
| Post-remediation check | Evidence against agreed completion criteria | Any areas outside that scope and the occupant’s clinical needs |

sections.heading: Agree the output and the end point
sections.markdown:
Decide who needs to use the report before accepting the quote. An owner arranging a repair, an insurer, a legal adviser and a clinician may need different information. Confirm whether the fee buys verbal advice, a short findings note, a laboratory result alone or an interpreted report with locations, limitations and recommendations. A data sheet with no explanation may leave the original decision unanswered.

For remediation, define the work and verification arrangements before cleanup begins where practicable. Ask who sets the acceptance criteria, who performs the work and who checks the result. A separate verifier can help manage conflicts of interest, but independence alone does not make an unsuitable method adequate. Distinguish completion of cleaning from correction of the moisture source, drying and any necessary building repair.

sections.heading: Keep investigation separate from product sales
sections.markdown:
Ask whether the assessor also supplies treatment, filtration, shielding, remediation or an affiliated product. A commercial relationship does not by itself invalidate an observation; it makes the rationale for the next purchase worth examining. Request the evidence, alternatives, intended outcome and how success will be assessed before authorising expensive follow-on work.

A qualification supports questions about training. It does not validate every health claim or every service sold under the same business name. Match the practitioner's experience and authorisations to the actual task, and check the laboratory's relevant analytical scope where testing is proposed. For suspected asbestos, lead, structural damage or medical symptoms, confirm the appropriate specialist pathway rather than assuming a broad healthy-home package covers it.

sections.heading: Build the complete fee from its components
sections.markdown: Ask for site attendance, report, sample collection, laboratory analysis, travel, tax treatment and any return visit as separate inclusions or charges. Agree how additional sampling will be authorised. A low initial inspection fee can become a much larger engagement if the document you need and several analyses are separately charged. Keep diagnostic work, remediation and later verification in distinct budget lines.

sections.heading: Worked example: a sample package and an unresolved leak
sections.markdown:
**Illustrative reasoning example, not an inspected property.** An owner has repeated growth behind a wardrobe after a roof leak. One quote emphasises several air samples; another includes a moisture investigation and asks for the roof-repair records. The owner wants to know whether the room can be used normally and whether the repair worked.

Separate the questions. Building evidence is needed to assess continuing moisture and affected materials. Any sampling should have a defined role in the investigation or verification plan. A laboratory result alone cannot confirm a roof repair or provide medical clearance for an individual occupant. Discuss health concerns with an appropriate clinician.

Compare the proposed methods and deliverables against those needs, including any concealed-area limits and follow-up. If the moisture source is still active, commissioning a larger sample package does not replace addressing it. If it has been rectified, agree how remaining effects and completion will be assessed rather than assuming the absence of visible growth settles every question.

The value lies in a defined question, an appropriate method and an interpretable result. A service label, alarming reading or extensive equipment list cannot supply those on its own.

> Important: Seek medical advice for symptoms, urgent health advice for significant exposure concerns and appropriately qualified building advice for defects.

faqs.question: What is a home environmental assessment?
faqs.answer: Usually an inspection by a building biologist or similar consultant focused on moisture, mould, ventilation and indoor air, and sometimes other factors such as electromagnetic fields. Ask what will be measured, what the results can and cannot show, and how findings are tied to building causes.

faqs.question: How much does a building biologist cost in Australia?
faqs.answer: Published examples checked on 7 September 2026 included $850 to $1,000 before samples and a detailed report, $990 before laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660. The final cost depends heavily on the samples, report and property scope.

faqs.question: What should a building biologist quote include?
faqs.answer: Request site time, rooms or areas, investigation methods, moisture mapping, sample count, laboratory fees, written report, travel, urgency and any return verification as separate line items.

faqs.question: What qualification can I check?
faqs.answer: The National Training Register lists 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology as current. Verify the individual’s relevant training, experience and authority for the actual task; the qualification does not confer medical registration.

faqs.question: Can a building biologist diagnose why someone is unwell?
faqs.answer: A registered health practitioner diagnoses and treats health conditions. An environmental consultant can investigate and measure defined building conditions.

faqs.question: Is EMF testing evidence that a home caused symptoms?
faqs.answer: Measurement can be compared with an identified exposure standard. Medical causation belongs with a health practitioner. ARPANSA is the Australian authority for radiation protection guidance.

faqs.question: Should I get mould testing before buying?
faqs.answer: Use testing for a defined question that can change the purchase decision or remediation scope. First identify visible moisture, leaks and affected materials through the appropriate building inspection.

faqs.question: Does every mould concern need laboratory testing?
faqs.answer: No. NSW Health says testing is generally unnecessary for visible household mould. Complex, concealed or formal verification questions may justify specialist assessment and a defined sampling plan.

faqs.question: Can a laboratory result certify the whole house as healthy?
faqs.answer: It describes the submitted sample and method. Building-wide conclusions need appropriate context and scope; individual health questions require clinical assessment.

faqs.question: Should the assessor also carry out the remediation?
faqs.answer: Ask about financial relationships and how scope and completion will be independently assessed where appropriate. Consider competence, method and conflicts of interest together.

| Where is water entering or condensing? | Building inspector, building consultant or suitably experienced moisture investigator | Moisture pathway, affected materials, access limits and repair brief |
| What is present in air, dust or a surface? | Indoor environmental professional or occupational hygienist with an appropriate sampling plan | Defined method, chain of custody, laboratory result and interpretation limits |
| Has mould remediation achieved its scope? | Independent post-remediation verifier | Pre-agreed acceptance criteria and verification report |
| Are symptoms connected with the home? | Registered health practitioner | Medical assessment informed by relevant building results |
| Is cracking, movement or another defect structurally significant? | Building inspector, then structural engineer if indicated | Building evidence and, where required, engineering diagnosis |

## Dated published pricing
These three provider pages were checked on 7 September 2026. They describe different packages, not a national price range. Provider prices are reported here as commercial observations; their inclusion is not an endorsement of a provider’s health claims or testing recommendations.

**Provider fee examples checked 7 September 2026; confirm tax treatment and address-specific scope**

| Provider example | Published fee | Important inclusions or additions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Building Biology NSW](https://buildingbiologynsw.com.au/service/the-complete-healthy-home-inspection/) | $850 single storey; up to $1,000 double storey | $140 per sample; comprehensive report separately $850; confirm GST and other charges |
| [Wave Building Biology](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) | $990 including GST | Mould assessment $990 including GST; sample analysis $120 each; confirm tax basis of extras |
| [Buildingbiology Services Australia](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) | About $970 standard; $1,660 detailed | Specified samples and reporting; travel additional. Confirm laboratory inclusions and GST for the selected package |

Property size, access, site time, sample count, laboratory fees, travel, report depth, urgency and return visits determine the final cost. Give each consultant the same written problem and ask for the complete expected fee.

## The quote checklist
- **Question and scope:** the rooms, history, suspected pathway and decision the report must support.
- **Investigation method:** visual inspection, moisture meter, thermal imaging, borescope, sampling or another defined method, and its limitations.
- **Sampling plan:** sample type, number, locations, controls, independent laboratory, chain of custody and the fee for each additional sample.
- **Deliverable:** verbal advice, short findings, comprehensive report, repair scope or post-remediation criteria.
- **Independence:** whether the assessor also sells remediation, products or follow-on work.
- **Professional standing:** relevant training, experience, professional indemnity and the laboratory’s accreditation for the analysis requested.

## Check training and laboratory scope
The [National Training Register lists 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology as current](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT). Verify the practitioner’s actual training and experience for the service commissioned. A qualification is not medical registration or blanket authority for every specialist task. For testing, check the laboratory’s relevant analytical scope and require the method, sample provenance and interpretation limits.

## Mould: find moisture before chasing species
Mould growth requires moisture. [NSW Health](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx) and the [Victorian Department of Health](https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/mould-and-your-health) emphasise moisture control and safe clean-up. Use sampling for a defined purpose such as characterising contamination, documenting a dispute or checking remediation.

[NSW Health says testing is generally unnecessary for visible household mould](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx), while concealed or unresolved problems can warrant specialist assessment. A DIY culture result alone cannot establish the source, full extent or individual health significance. Start with [the moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home) and a defined question.

## EMF measurement and health questions
An instrument can measure an electromagnetic field, but the quantity, frequency, method and comparison standard must fit the question. [ARPANSA states that evidence does not establish low-level EMF exposure as the cause of attributed hypersensitivity symptoms](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/understanding-radiation/radiation-sources/more-radiation-sources/electromagnetic-hypersensitivity), while recognising that symptoms are real and recommending medical assessment. A measured field is not evidence that a home caused illness. Do not treat a consultant’s private target as an Australian exposure standard.

## When specialist environmental work is proportionate
- **Recurring or widespread mould** where the water source or affected extent remains unclear.
- **A concealed or complex water event**, including a flood, long-running leak or contaminated cavity.
- **A formal dispute, insurance or remediation process** that needs an agreed sampling or verification protocol.
- **A vulnerable occupant** where a health practitioner wants better environmental information to support clinical care.
- **A specific exposure question** that can be measured against a recognised method and standard.

For an ordinary pre-purchase decision, start with a qualified [building and pest inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). Add environmental work for specific questions left unresolved.

## Decide what a sample could change before buying it
Write the question before choosing the test. Are you trying to find a moisture source, characterise a particular material, document the extent of contamination or check an agreed remediation outcome? Ask how the proposed sample and method answer that question, what comparison is appropriate and what an inconclusive result would mean. A package with more samples is not automatically a more useful investigation.

Keep the field context with the laboratory result in your [home record](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/keeping-a-record-of-your-home): date, room or location, material, recent cleaning or disturbance, sampling method and relevant conditions. Ask the assessor what the sample represents and what it does not. A result from one sampled location should not quietly become a conclusion about every concealed part of a building or the cause of an occupant's symptoms.

**A result and the separate decision it leaves open**

| Evidence | What it may contribute | What still needs assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visible staining or growth | A location and extent to investigate | Moisture source, concealed effects and appropriate response |
| Laboratory result | Information about the submitted sample using the stated method | Representativeness, interpretation and building-wide significance |
| Instrument reading | A measured quantity under particular conditions | Whether the method and comparison answer the original question |
| Post-remediation check | Evidence against agreed completion criteria | Any areas outside that scope and the occupant’s clinical needs |

## Agree the output and the end point
Decide who needs to use the report before accepting the quote. An owner arranging a repair, an insurer, a legal adviser and a clinician may need different information. Confirm whether the fee buys verbal advice, a short findings note, a laboratory result alone or an interpreted report with locations, limitations and recommendations. A data sheet with no explanation may leave the original decision unanswered.

For remediation, define the work and verification arrangements before cleanup begins where practicable. Ask who sets the acceptance criteria, who performs the work and who checks the result. A separate verifier can help manage conflicts of interest, but independence alone does not make an unsuitable method adequate. Distinguish completion of cleaning from correction of the moisture source, drying and any necessary building repair.

## Keep investigation separate from product sales
Ask whether the assessor also supplies treatment, filtration, shielding, remediation or an affiliated product. A commercial relationship does not by itself invalidate an observation; it makes the rationale for the next purchase worth examining. Request the evidence, alternatives, intended outcome and how success will be assessed before authorising expensive follow-on work.

A qualification supports questions about training. It does not validate every health claim or every service sold under the same business name. Match the practitioner's experience and authorisations to the actual task, and check the laboratory's relevant analytical scope where testing is proposed. For suspected asbestos, lead, structural damage or medical symptoms, confirm the appropriate specialist pathway rather than assuming a broad healthy-home package covers it.

## Build the complete fee from its components
Ask for site attendance, report, sample collection, laboratory analysis, travel, tax treatment and any return visit as separate inclusions or charges. Agree how additional sampling will be authorised. A low initial inspection fee can become a much larger engagement if the document you need and several analyses are separately charged. Keep diagnostic work, remediation and later verification in distinct budget lines.

## Worked example: a sample package and an unresolved leak
**Illustrative reasoning example, not an inspected property.** An owner has repeated growth behind a wardrobe after a roof leak. One quote emphasises several air samples; another includes a moisture investigation and asks for the roof-repair records. The owner wants to know whether the room can be used normally and whether the repair worked.

Separate the questions. Building evidence is needed to assess continuing moisture and affected materials. Any sampling should have a defined role in the investigation or verification plan. A laboratory result alone cannot confirm a roof repair or provide medical clearance for an individual occupant. Discuss health concerns with an appropriate clinician.

Compare the proposed methods and deliverables against those needs, including any concealed-area limits and follow-up. If the moisture source is still active, commissioning a larger sample package does not replace addressing it. If it has been rectified, agree how remaining effects and completion will be assessed rather than assuming the absence of visible growth settles every question.

The value lies in a defined question, an appropriate method and an interpretable result. A service label, alarming reading or extensive equipment list cannot supply those on its own.

> Important: Seek medical advice for symptoms, urgent health advice for significant exposure concerns and appropriately qualified building advice for defects.

## Frequently asked questions
### What is a home environmental assessment?
Usually an inspection by a building biologist or similar consultant focused on moisture, mould, ventilation and indoor air, and sometimes other factors such as electromagnetic fields. Ask what will be measured, what the results can and cannot show, and how findings are tied to building causes.

### How much does a building biologist cost in Australia?
Published examples checked on 7 September 2026 included $850 to $1,000 before samples and a detailed report, $990 before laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660. The final cost depends heavily on the samples, report and property scope.

### What should a building biologist quote include?
Request site time, rooms or areas, investigation methods, moisture mapping, sample count, laboratory fees, written report, travel, urgency and any return verification as separate line items.

### What qualification can I check?
The National Training Register lists 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology as current. Verify the individual’s relevant training, experience and authority for the actual task; the qualification does not confer medical registration.

### Can a building biologist diagnose why someone is unwell?
A registered health practitioner diagnoses and treats health conditions. An environmental consultant can investigate and measure defined building conditions.

### Is EMF testing evidence that a home caused symptoms?
Measurement can be compared with an identified exposure standard. Medical causation belongs with a health practitioner. ARPANSA is the Australian authority for radiation protection guidance.

### Should I get mould testing before buying?
Use testing for a defined question that can change the purchase decision or remediation scope. First identify visible moisture, leaks and affected materials through the appropriate building inspection.

### Does every mould concern need laboratory testing?
No. NSW Health says testing is generally unnecessary for visible household mould. Complex, concealed or formal verification questions may justify specialist assessment and a defined sampling plan.

### Can a laboratory result certify the whole house as healthy?
It describes the submitted sample and method. Building-wide conclusions need appropriate context and scope; individual health questions require clinical assessment.

### Should the assessor also carry out the remediation?
Ask about financial relationships and how scope and completion will be independently assessed where appropriate. Consider competence, method and conflicts of interest together.

## Method
A scoped-service and evidence guide using provider prices only for fee components. Health and exposure statements are grounded in public-health authorities; sampling results are separated from medical diagnosis and remediation decisions.

## Limitations
Take health concerns to a registered health practitioner and structural concerns to an appropriately qualified building professional.

## Sources

- [Prices](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) — Wave Building Biology; accessed 2026-09-07
- [Mould inspection fees](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) — Buildingbiology Services Australia; accessed 2026-09-07

guides.question: What is the cooling-off period when buying property by state?
guides.title: Property cooling-off periods by state: the Australian comparison
guides.summary: Property cooling-off periods in every Australian state and territory: the number of days, when the clock starts, and the auction exceptions.
guides.answer: The headline period is five business days in NSW and Queensland, five working days in the ACT, four business days in the NT, three clear business days in Victoria and two clear business days in South Australia. Ordinary private sales in WA and Tasmania have no general statutory period. Ask your conveyancer or solicitor to confirm when your clock starts, when it ends, what exceptions apply and how notice must be given.
guides.methodology: A sourced jurisdiction comparison followed by a practical deadline record. Eligibility, statutory withdrawal and negotiated conditions are kept separate; the fictional scenario does not calculate a reader’s legal deadline.
guides.limitations: Legal orientation only. Property type, buyer identity, auction timing, certificates, written waivers and contract terms can change the result.
guides.researchNote: Each jurisdiction in the comparison links to its official guidance or primary legislation. Eligibility and prescribed mechanisms matter as much as the day count. The ACT reference is sections 12–15 of the current linked republication; the hypothetical deadline example illustrates workflow, not a legal calculation.

cluster.label: How to buy
cluster.blurb: Sequence the checks, understand their limits and be ready before your offer becomes binding.

sections.heading: Opening
sections.markdown:
### Know when your clock starts and stops
- **Trigger:** Signing, exchange or receipt: each state picks its own starting gun
- **Deadline:** Counted in clear, business or working days, and it matters which
- **Exceptions:** Auctions, waivers and edge cases can switch it off entirely

_Get your actual deadline, for your actual contract, in writing._

sections.heading: The state-by-state orientation
sections.markdown:
This table covers the usual residential private-sale position for an individual buyer. Auctions, off-the-plan contracts, options, corporate buyers, rural or commercial land, written waivers and contract amendments can change the result. Have the actual deadline confirmed.

**Residential cooling-off orientation, legal review is still required for the actual contract**

| State / territory | Headline period | Typical consequence of withdrawal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [NSW](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) | 5 business days after exchange; 10 business days for off-the-plan contracts | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [VIC](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/buying-property-by-private-sale) | 3 clear business days, beginning when the buyer signs | The greater of $100 or 0.2% of the purchase price |
| [QLD](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts) | 5 business days, triggered by the buyer receiving the fully signed contract | Seller may deduct up to 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [ACT](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/a/2003-40/current/PDF/2003-40.PDF) | 5 working days | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [NT](https://nt.gov.au/property/buying-and-selling-a-home/get-help-with-the-contract/contract-of-sale) | 4 business days in the usual eligible transaction | Eligible cooling-off cancellation without penalty, according to NT Government guidance |
| [SA](https://lsc.sa.gov.au/handbook/ch23s08s08s01.php) | 2 clear business days; the Form 1 timing matters | Any deposit paid above $100 must be refunded on eligible cooling-off cancellation |
| [WA](https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/buying-property-private-sale) | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |
| [TAS](https://cbos.tas.gov.au/topics/housing/buying-selling-property/advice-buying-selling-property) | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |

sections.heading: Each state starts the clock differently
sections.markdown:
The headline length is only half of the rule. The start point, the counting method and the final-day cutoff also differ, so read the rule for the state where the property is.

### Cooling-off period in Victoria

In Victoria, the [three-clear-business-day period begins on the date the buyer signs](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/buying-property-by-private-sale). A buyer who withdraws usually forfeits the greater of $100 or 0.2% of the purchase price.

### Cooling-off period in NSW

In NSW, the [five-business-day period starts at exchange](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) and ends at 5 pm on the fifth business day after the day of exchange. Off-the-plan contracts generally have ten business days, and withdrawing usually costs 0.25% of the purchase price.

### Cooling-off period in Queensland

In Queensland, the [clock starts when the buyer receives the contract signed by both parties](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts). The seller may deduct up to 0.25% of the purchase price if the buyer withdraws.

Queensland's receipt rule includes receipt by a representative; a contract arriving on a weekend or public holiday starts the period on the next business day. Its final-day cutoff is 5 pm. Keep the delivery evidence and have the actual count checked under [Queensland's rules](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts).

### Cooling-off period in South Australia, the ACT and the NT

In South Australia, the [two-clear-business-day period follows signing or service of Form 1, whichever is later](https://www.sa.gov.au/topics/housing/buying-building-selling/selling-a-property/selling-your-home). In the ACT, [section 12](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/a/2003-40/current/PDF/2003-40.PDF) starts the period when the contract is made and sets expiry at 5 pm on the fifth working day after that day, subject to its exclusions and permitted changes. [NT guidance](https://nt.gov.au/property/buying-and-selling-a-home/get-help-with-the-contract/contract-of-sale) ties its four-business-day period to final signing and exchange. Have your own expiry confirmed rather than transferring another state's counting rule.

sections.heading: Auction and near-auction exceptions
sections.markdown:
A purchase made at auction generally has no cooling-off period. The edges differ. Victoria also excludes a private sale made within three clear business days before or after a publicly advertised auction. NSW excludes exchange on the auction day after the property is passed in. Queensland excludes a follow-up sale after an unsuccessful auction if it occurs before 5 pm on the second business day and the buyer was a registered bidder. Those rules are why an auction calendar can matter even when the final negotiation looks like a private sale.

If an auction is in the picture, finish the contract, finance and building work before you bid. Use the [auction due-diligence checklist](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence) and the narrower guide to [pre-auction building inspections](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-inspection-before-auction).

sections.heading: Waiving, shortening or changing the period
sections.markdown: Some regimes allow the buyer to waive or shorten the period through a prescribed mechanism. [NSW uses a section 66W certificate](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) from the buyer's solicitor or conveyancer. [Queensland permits a written waiver or shortening](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts). A waiver removes or shortens the buyer's statutory cooling-off right, so the right to rescind may end as soon as the prescribed waiver takes effect.

sections.heading: Contract conditions in WA and Tasmania
sections.markdown: WA and Tasmania have no general statutory cooling-off period for ordinary private sales. Use appropriately drafted contract conditions for finance, building and pest, sale of another property or due diligence. The [WA Government advises buyers to understand the contract before signing](https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/buying-property-private-sale). Have each condition drafted or reviewed professionally.

sections.heading: What to do inside a cooling-off window
sections.markdown:
1. **Have the contract and disclosure bundle reviewed**, including title, plan, easements, covenants, planning controls, notices and settlement terms.
2. **Confirm finance against this property**, including valuation or lender conditions still outstanding.
3. **Complete the physical checks** the property warrants within the available time.
4. **Escalate specific flags** to an engineer, electrician, plumber, strata specialist or other appropriate professional.
5. **Keep the deadline and notice method in writing**, using the method your legal representative confirms.

sections.heading: Keep four separate rights and dates apart
sections.markdown:
Cooling-off, a finance condition, an inspection condition and rights arising from defective disclosure are different legal questions. A contract may have one without another. Finding a defect does not by itself tell you which right is available, what evidence it requires or how to exercise it. Give the actual finding and contract to your legal adviser before treating 'subject to inspection' as permission to leave for any reason. Read the relevant disclosure bundle alongside that advice: [Victoria’s Section 32 vendor statement](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/reading-a-section-32), the [NSW contract for sale](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/reading-a-contract-for-sale-nsw) or [Queensland’s Form 2](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/seller-disclosure-qld).

Each condition can have its own deadline, notice requirements and consequences. A lender still considering an application does not automatically extend the finance condition, and a delayed inspection does not automatically extend cooling-off. Keep a separate entry for each right rather than a single calendar event labelled 'contract goes unconditional'. Ask what happens if one deadline passes while another remains open.

sections.heading: Create a deadline record from the actual transaction
sections.markdown:
**Ask your legal adviser to confirm these fields**

| Field | What to record | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eligibility | Property type, buyer identity, sale method and relevant exclusions | The headline period may not apply |
| Trigger | The legally relevant signing, exchange, receipt or service event and evidence of it | A different event can produce a different date |
| Expiry | Date, time, applicable public holidays and any agreed alteration | Business days and clear business days require the correct counting rule |
| Notice | Who must sign, recipient, permitted method and service requirements | Deciding to withdraw is not the same as effective notice |
| Money | Applicable deduction, deposit treatment and your own incurred fees | Cooling off may still have a cost |
| Action owner | Who is instructed to act and how confirmation will be obtained | Sending a report for review is not necessarily an instruction to terminate |

Keep the signed version, exchange or delivery correspondence, waiver documents and any agreed extension together. If you are travelling or the property is interstate, ask the adviser to state the relevant local time. Do not rely on a generic date calculator where eligibility, public holidays, delivery or document wording is disputed.

sections.heading: An extension request is not an extension
sections.markdown:
If an essential report will arrive too late, tell your adviser early enough to assess the options. These may include seeking an agreed extension, exercising an available right or proceeding with the uncertainty understood. The seller may decline the request. Continue working to the existing deadline until your adviser confirms a valid change; neither silence nor a reassuring conversation should be treated as one.

A report received before expiry may still require clarification or specialist follow-up. Work backwards from the decision and the time needed to give any effective notice, rather than booking the inspection for the last available slot. Use the [report-reading guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/how-to-read-a-building-and-pest-report) to identify the question requiring a decision, while your adviser handles the legal pathway.

sections.heading: Price the exit using the correct base
sections.markdown:
Where a percentage deduction applies, check whether it is calculated on the purchase price rather than the amount of deposit paid. For illustration, 0.25% of an $800,000 purchase price is $2,000, regardless of whether the initial deposit was smaller than the usual deposit. This arithmetic does not establish that the deduction applies to your contract. Your legal, inspection and other costs may also have been incurred.

If the period has expired or been waived, seek advice about the actual contract and circumstances. Do not assume the cooling-off deduction remains an optional cancellation fee. Other exit rights, if any, have their own requirements, and failing to complete can have different consequences.

sections.heading: Worked example: the report comes after the confirmed deadline
sections.markdown:
**Illustrative reasoning example, not an inspected property.** A buyer's solicitor confirms that their cooling-off right expires at 5 pm on Tuesday. An inspector can deliver a moisture investigation on Wednesday. The agent says they will ask the seller for more time, and the buyer assumes the problem is solved.

The report booking, request for time and legal deadline are three different facts. Until the solicitor confirms an effective extension, Tuesday remains the working deadline. Ask the solicitor to explain the available options and required instructions while there is still time to act.

If an extension is agreed, record the new terms and allow time to interpret the report. If it is declined, the buyer must make a decision with the uncertainty visible. A later report may be useful evidence about the building, but its arrival does not itself reopen an expired right.

> Important: Legal sources reviewed on 7 September 2026. Have a conveyancer or solicitor confirm eligibility, the exact expiry time, effective notice and the financial consequence for your contract. This comparison is not a personalised deadline calculation.

faqs.question: How long is the cooling-off period when buying a house?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state and the contract: from five business days in NSW and Queensland down to none at all for ordinary private sales in WA and Tasmania. Have the trigger, the exact deadline and the exclusions confirmed for your contract.

faqs.question: Is there a cooling-off period at auction?
faqs.answer: Cooling-off is generally unavailable at auction. Some states also exclude defined transactions close to an auction.

faqs.question: When does the cooling-off clock start?
faqs.answer: Victoria starts when the buyer signs, NSW at exchange, and Queensland when the buyer receives the contract signed by both parties. South Australia’s Form 1 timing also matters.

faqs.question: Can a cooling-off period be waived?
faqs.answer: In some jurisdictions, yes, using a prescribed or written mechanism. NSW uses a section 66W certificate; Queensland permits written waiver or shortening. Take legal advice because a waiver can remove or shorten the buyer’s statutory right to rescind.

faqs.question: What if the state has no statutory cooling-off period?
faqs.answer: Negotiate appropriate conditions into the contract before signing and have them professionally drafted or reviewed. In WA and Tasmania, contract conditions usually do the protective work a statutory cooling-off period performs elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does a delayed inspection extend cooling-off?
faqs.answer: No automatic extension follows from a delay. Ask your legal adviser about the available options and continue to work to the existing deadline until a valid change is confirmed.

faqs.question: Is the cooling-off deduction a percentage of my deposit?
faqs.answer: Where a percentage applies, it is generally expressed against the purchase price in the jurisdictions listed here. Confirm the applicable rule and deposit treatment for your contract.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw because the building report found a defect?
faqs.answer: That depends on an available cooling-off right, the terms of any inspection condition or another applicable legal right. A defect alone does not identify the correct termination pathway.

faqs.question: Does a finance clause replace cooling-off?
faqs.answer: No. It is a separate contractual protection with its own terms and deadline. Have both reviewed and recorded separately.

guides.contentMarkdown:
# Property cooling-off periods by state: the Australian comparison

The headline period is five business days in NSW and Queensland, five working days in the ACT, four business days in the NT, three clear business days in Victoria and two clear business days in South Australia. Ordinary private sales in WA and Tasmania have no general statutory period. Ask your conveyancer or solicitor to confirm when your clock starts, when it ends, what exceptions apply and how notice must be given.

## Research note
Each jurisdiction in the comparison links to its official guidance or primary legislation. Eligibility and prescribed mechanisms matter as much as the day count. The ACT reference is sections 12–15 of the current linked republication; the hypothetical deadline example illustrates workflow, not a legal calculation.

## Opening
### Know when your clock starts and stops
- **Trigger:** Signing, exchange or receipt: each state picks its own starting gun
- **Deadline:** Counted in clear, business or working days, and it matters which
- **Exceptions:** Auctions, waivers and edge cases can switch it off entirely

_Get your actual deadline, for your actual contract, in writing._

## The state-by-state orientation
This table covers the usual residential private-sale position for an individual buyer. Auctions, off-the-plan contracts, options, corporate buyers, rural or commercial land, written waivers and contract amendments can change the result. Have the actual deadline confirmed.

**Residential cooling-off orientation, legal review is still required for the actual contract**

| State / territory | Headline period | Typical consequence of withdrawal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [NSW](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) | 5 business days after exchange; 10 business days for off-the-plan contracts | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [VIC](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/buying-property-by-private-sale) | 3 clear business days, beginning when the buyer signs | The greater of $100 or 0.2% of the purchase price |
| [QLD](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts) | 5 business days, triggered by the buyer receiving the fully signed contract | Seller may deduct up to 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [ACT](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/a/2003-40/current/PDF/2003-40.PDF) | 5 working days | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| [NT](https://nt.gov.au/property/buying-and-selling-a-home/get-help-with-the-contract/contract-of-sale) | 4 business days in the usual eligible transaction | Eligible cooling-off cancellation without penalty, according to NT Government guidance |
| [SA](https://lsc.sa.gov.au/handbook/ch23s08s08s01.php) | 2 clear business days; the Form 1 timing matters | Any deposit paid above $100 must be refunded on eligible cooling-off cancellation |
| [WA](https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/buying-property-private-sale) | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |
| [TAS](https://cbos.tas.gov.au/topics/housing/buying-selling-property/advice-buying-selling-property) | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |

## Each state starts the clock differently
The headline length is only half of the rule. The start point, the counting method and the final-day cutoff also differ, so read the rule for the state where the property is.

### Cooling-off period in Victoria

In Victoria, the [three-clear-business-day period begins on the date the buyer signs](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/buying-property-by-private-sale). A buyer who withdraws usually forfeits the greater of $100 or 0.2% of the purchase price.

### Cooling-off period in NSW

In NSW, the [five-business-day period starts at exchange](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) and ends at 5 pm on the fifth business day after the day of exchange. Off-the-plan contracts generally have ten business days, and withdrawing usually costs 0.25% of the purchase price.

### Cooling-off period in Queensland

In Queensland, the [clock starts when the buyer receives the contract signed by both parties](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts). The seller may deduct up to 0.25% of the purchase price if the buyer withdraws.

Queensland's receipt rule includes receipt by a representative; a contract arriving on a weekend or public holiday starts the period on the next business day. Its final-day cutoff is 5 pm. Keep the delivery evidence and have the actual count checked under [Queensland's rules](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts).

### Cooling-off period in South Australia, the ACT and the NT

In South Australia, the [two-clear-business-day period follows signing or service of Form 1, whichever is later](https://www.sa.gov.au/topics/housing/buying-building-selling/selling-a-property/selling-your-home). In the ACT, [section 12](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/a/2003-40/current/PDF/2003-40.PDF) starts the period when the contract is made and sets expiry at 5 pm on the fifth working day after that day, subject to its exclusions and permitted changes. [NT guidance](https://nt.gov.au/property/buying-and-selling-a-home/get-help-with-the-contract/contract-of-sale) ties its four-business-day period to final signing and exchange. Have your own expiry confirmed rather than transferring another state's counting rule.

## Auction and near-auction exceptions
A purchase made at auction generally has no cooling-off period. The edges differ. Victoria also excludes a private sale made within three clear business days before or after a publicly advertised auction. NSW excludes exchange on the auction day after the property is passed in. Queensland excludes a follow-up sale after an unsuccessful auction if it occurs before 5 pm on the second business day and the buyer was a registered bidder. Those rules are why an auction calendar can matter even when the final negotiation looks like a private sale.

If an auction is in the picture, finish the contract, finance and building work before you bid. Use the [auction due-diligence checklist](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence) and the narrower guide to [pre-auction building inspections](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-inspection-before-auction).

## Waiving, shortening or changing the period
Some regimes allow the buyer to waive or shorten the period through a prescribed mechanism. [NSW uses a section 66W certificate](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) from the buyer's solicitor or conveyancer. [Queensland permits a written waiver or shortening](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts). A waiver removes or shortens the buyer's statutory cooling-off right, so the right to rescind may end as soon as the prescribed waiver takes effect.

## Contract conditions in WA and Tasmania
WA and Tasmania have no general statutory cooling-off period for ordinary private sales. Use appropriately drafted contract conditions for finance, building and pest, sale of another property or due diligence. The [WA Government advises buyers to understand the contract before signing](https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/buying-property-private-sale). Have each condition drafted or reviewed professionally.

## What to do inside a cooling-off window
1. **Have the contract and disclosure bundle reviewed**, including title, plan, easements, covenants, planning controls, notices and settlement terms.
2. **Confirm finance against this property**, including valuation or lender conditions still outstanding.
3. **Complete the physical checks** the property warrants within the available time.
4. **Escalate specific flags** to an engineer, electrician, plumber, strata specialist or other appropriate professional.
5. **Keep the deadline and notice method in writing**, using the method your legal representative confirms.

## Keep four separate rights and dates apart
Cooling-off, a finance condition, an inspection condition and rights arising from defective disclosure are different legal questions. A contract may have one without another. Finding a defect does not by itself tell you which right is available, what evidence it requires or how to exercise it. Give the actual finding and contract to your legal adviser before treating 'subject to inspection' as permission to leave for any reason. Read the relevant disclosure bundle alongside that advice: [Victoria’s Section 32 vendor statement](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/reading-a-section-32), the [NSW contract for sale](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/reading-a-contract-for-sale-nsw) or [Queensland’s Form 2](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/seller-disclosure-qld).

Each condition can have its own deadline, notice requirements and consequences. A lender still considering an application does not automatically extend the finance condition, and a delayed inspection does not automatically extend cooling-off. Keep a separate entry for each right rather than a single calendar event labelled 'contract goes unconditional'. Ask what happens if one deadline passes while another remains open.

## Create a deadline record from the actual transaction
**Ask your legal adviser to confirm these fields**

| Field | What to record | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eligibility | Property type, buyer identity, sale method and relevant exclusions | The headline period may not apply |
| Trigger | The legally relevant signing, exchange, receipt or service event and evidence of it | A different event can produce a different date |
| Expiry | Date, time, applicable public holidays and any agreed alteration | Business days and clear business days require the correct counting rule |
| Notice | Who must sign, recipient, permitted method and service requirements | Deciding to withdraw is not the same as effective notice |
| Money | Applicable deduction, deposit treatment and your own incurred fees | Cooling off may still have a cost |
| Action owner | Who is instructed to act and how confirmation will be obtained | Sending a report for review is not necessarily an instruction to terminate |

Keep the signed version, exchange or delivery correspondence, waiver documents and any agreed extension together. If you are travelling or the property is interstate, ask the adviser to state the relevant local time. Do not rely on a generic date calculator where eligibility, public holidays, delivery or document wording is disputed.

## An extension request is not an extension
If an essential report will arrive too late, tell your adviser early enough to assess the options. These may include seeking an agreed extension, exercising an available right or proceeding with the uncertainty understood. The seller may decline the request. Continue working to the existing deadline until your adviser confirms a valid change; neither silence nor a reassuring conversation should be treated as one.

A report received before expiry may still require clarification or specialist follow-up. Work backwards from the decision and the time needed to give any effective notice, rather than booking the inspection for the last available slot. Use the [report-reading guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/how-to-read-a-building-and-pest-report) to identify the question requiring a decision, while your adviser handles the legal pathway.

## Price the exit using the correct base
Where a percentage deduction applies, check whether it is calculated on the purchase price rather than the amount of deposit paid. For illustration, 0.25% of an $800,000 purchase price is $2,000, regardless of whether the initial deposit was smaller than the usual deposit. This arithmetic does not establish that the deduction applies to your contract. Your legal, inspection and other costs may also have been incurred.

If the period has expired or been waived, seek advice about the actual contract and circumstances. Do not assume the cooling-off deduction remains an optional cancellation fee. Other exit rights, if any, have their own requirements, and failing to complete can have different consequences.

## Worked example: the report comes after the confirmed deadline
**Illustrative reasoning example, not an inspected property.** A buyer's solicitor confirms that their cooling-off right expires at 5 pm on Tuesday. An inspector can deliver a moisture investigation on Wednesday. The agent says they will ask the seller for more time, and the buyer assumes the problem is solved.

The report booking, request for time and legal deadline are three different facts. Until the solicitor confirms an effective extension, Tuesday remains the working deadline. Ask the solicitor to explain the available options and required instructions while there is still time to act.

If an extension is agreed, record the new terms and allow time to interpret the report. If it is declined, the buyer must make a decision with the uncertainty visible. A later report may be useful evidence about the building, but its arrival does not itself reopen an expired right.

> Important: Legal sources reviewed on 7 September 2026. Have a conveyancer or solicitor confirm eligibility, the exact expiry time, effective notice and the financial consequence for your contract. This comparison is not a personalised deadline calculation.

## Frequently asked questions
### How long is the cooling-off period when buying a house?
It depends on the state and the contract: from five business days in NSW and Queensland down to none at all for ordinary private sales in WA and Tasmania. Have the trigger, the exact deadline and the exclusions confirmed for your contract.

### Is there a cooling-off period at auction?
Cooling-off is generally unavailable at auction. Some states also exclude defined transactions close to an auction.

### When does the cooling-off clock start?
Victoria starts when the buyer signs, NSW at exchange, and Queensland when the buyer receives the contract signed by both parties. South Australia’s Form 1 timing also matters.

### Can a cooling-off period be waived?
In some jurisdictions, yes, using a prescribed or written mechanism. NSW uses a section 66W certificate; Queensland permits written waiver or shortening. Take legal advice because a waiver can remove or shorten the buyer’s statutory right to rescind.

### What if the state has no statutory cooling-off period?
Negotiate appropriate conditions into the contract before signing and have them professionally drafted or reviewed. In WA and Tasmania, contract conditions usually do the protective work a statutory cooling-off period performs elsewhere.

### Does a delayed inspection extend cooling-off?
No automatic extension follows from a delay. Ask your legal adviser about the available options and continue to work to the existing deadline until a valid change is confirmed.

### Is the cooling-off deduction a percentage of my deposit?
Where a percentage applies, it is generally expressed against the purchase price in the jurisdictions listed here. Confirm the applicable rule and deposit treatment for your contract.

### Can I withdraw because the building report found a defect?
That depends on an available cooling-off right, the terms of any inspection condition or another applicable legal right. A defect alone does not identify the correct termination pathway.

### Does a finance clause replace cooling-off?
No. It is a separate contractual protection with its own terms and deadline. Have both reviewed and recorded separately.

## Method
A sourced jurisdiction comparison followed by a practical deadline record. Eligibility, statutory withdrawal and negotiated conditions are kept separate; the fictional scenario does not calculate a reader’s legal deadline.

## Limitations
Legal orientation only. Property type, buyer identity, auction timing, certificates, written waivers and contract terms can change the result.

guides.question: What due diligence should I do before bidding at auction?
guides.title: Auction-day due diligence: the buyer's checklist
guides.summary: A good auction plan is finished before the crowd arrives. Clear the contract, building, finance, deposit and price-limit questions, then keep your written limit where you can see it.
guides.answer: Before you bid, have the contract and disclosure reviewed, put any agreed changes in writing and understand the building report, including the areas it could not cover. Ask your lender or broker how valuation, property type and the final price affect approval. Check how the deposit must be paid and write down a hard limit that already includes the immediate work and buying costs.
guides.methodology: A pre-bid decision guide separating completed checks, bounded allowances and unresolved dependencies. State auction examples are explicitly local; legal and lending questions remain with the relevant advisers.
guides.limitations: General Australian guidance only. Contracts, statutes, policies, site conditions and professional scopes vary; obtain advice for the property and decision in front of you.
